Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service San Diego CA
135 AM PST Tue Nov 24 2026

.SYNOPSIS...
Widespread coastal flooding is expected this week due to King 
Tides and increased surf. Today will be warmer with weak offshore 
flow. Winds will weaken on Wednesday with a brief return to 
onshore flow. Thanksgiving and Friday will be dry and warmer with 
northeast winds gusting to 35 to 45 mph along and below the 
coastal slopes of the mountains and through passes. A cooling 
trend is expected for Saturday into early next week. The next 
chance of precipitation is for late Sunday into Monday. A more 
substantial storm with heavier precipitation is possible for next 
Tuesday and Wednesday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...FOR EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA INCLUDING ORANGE...
SAN DIEGO...WESTERN RIVERSIDE AND SOUTHWESTERN SAN BERNARDINO
COUNTIES...

.SHORT TERM (Today through Thursday)...
There will be weak offshore flow today with east winds gusting to
35 mph along and below the coastal slopes of the mountains in
Riverside and San Diego Counties. High temperatures for the coast,
valleys, and coastal slopes of the mountains will warm 4 to 8
degrees with the deserts a few degrees warmer. High temperatures
for the coast and valleys will be mostly in the 70s today.

A weak low pressure system moving inland through Baja and southern
California on Wednesday will weaken the offshore flow. Not much
change is expected with high temperatures for the coast and
valleys with the deserts a few degrees warmer.

For Thanksgiving and Friday, strengthening high pressure aloft 
and stronger offshore flow will bring warming with gusty northeast
to east winds along and below the coastal slopes of the 
mountains. High temperatures on Thanksgiving will warm 4 to 8 
degrees for the coast and valleys with the deserts around 5 
degrees warmer. High temperatures will be 10 to 15 degrees above 
average for the coast and western valleys on Thanksgiving. The 
warmest high temperatures on Thanksgiving will be in the lower to
mid 80s for inland coastal areas into the western valleys. 

&&

.LONG TERM (Friday through Monday)...
High temperatures on Friday will be slightly warmer near sea level
to around 5 degrees warmer for the mountains. High temperatures on
Friday will be around 80 near the coast with the valleys and 
inland coastal areas mostly in the lower to mid 80s.

High pressure aloft will weaken and onshore flow strengthen for
Saturday into early next week which will spread cooling inland.
High temperatures on Saturday for the coast and valleys will cool
5 to 10 degrees with high temperatures mostly in the 70s. High
temperatures on Sunday will cool another 5 degrees or so with high
temperatures for the coast and valleys mostly in the upper 60s to
mid 70s.

A low pressure system moving quickly inland through southern
California around Sunday could bring some precipitation for Sunday
into Sunday night. A more substantial storm with heavier
precipitation is possible for next Tuesday and Wednesday. For next
Tuesday and Wednesday, the chance for 1 inch or more of rainfall 
is 55 to 65 percent for the coast to the mountains. The chance for
2 inches or more of rainfall ranges from around 25 to 35 percent 
near the coast to 45 to 55 percent for the San Bernardino County 
mountains. The chance for 5 inches or more of rainfall is around 5
to 10 percent for the San Bernardino County mountains.

&&

.AVIATION... 
240600Z...SCT-BKN high clouds will move across tonight/early Tuesday 
morning, AOA 20,000ft MSL, clearing out late Tuesday morning. East 
winds gusting locally to 30 kts expected Tuesday morning over the 
coastal facing foothill slopes, weakening around 18z. 

Otherwise, VFR conditions prevail regionwide.

&&

.MARINE...
No hazardous marine conditions are expected through today.

A large, long period west swell will arrive Wednesday afternoon 
and build into Thursday, bringing combined seas of 8-12 feet. 
Northwest winds briefly reach 20-25 kt in the outer coastal waters
near San Clemente Island Wednesday afternoon and evening. The 
combination of large seas and breezy winds will create conditions 
hazardous to small craft. A Small Craft Advisory will be in effect 
for the outer waters from late Wednesday morning through late 
Thursday morning. Seas begin to wane Thursday afternoon, falling 
below 10 feet by Thursday evening.

&&

.BEACHES...
Morning high tides will increase this week, and already reached 7.73 
feet (MLLW) at La Jolla. Highest tides will occur Tuesday through 
Thursday at 7.9-8.3 feet, peaking on Wednesday. These forecast tides 
have been adjusted 1.1-1.2 feet above baseline astronomical 
predictions based on trends in recent observations, and will likely 
break the all time tidal records just recently set in late October. 

Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 2-5 feet 
through Wednesday morning, but an incoming west swell of 8-9 ft at 
18-19 seconds arrives late Wednesday into Thursday. This 
will generate large breaking waves of 6-8 feet on Thursday, with 
sets of 10-12 feet on exposed west-facing beaches. Surf lowers to 3-
6 feet on Friday. A High Surf Advisory has been issued for San Diego 
County as the west-northwest swell will focus the higher surf on the 
west-facing beaches.

The combination of forecast record high tides and elevated surf will 
bring moderate to locally major coastal flooding during Tuesday 
morning's high tide. A Coastal Flood Advisory remains in effect 
through early Tuesday morning. King Tides Tue-Thu combined with 
elevated to high surf bring major coastal flooding, with locally 
extreme flooding expected during Thursday morning's high tide. A 
Coastal Flood Warning remains in effect from this morning through
early Friday afternoon.

&&

.CLIMATE...
The peak water level of 8.24 feet at the San Diego Broadway Pier
on Monday morning was the fifth highest on record. It was also 
the second highest for November, exceeded by the 8.26 feet on 
November 25th, 2015. Three of the five highest water levels ever 
recorded at San Diego have occurred this year since July.

The highest water level ever recorded in San Diego was 8.52 feet
in late October of this year. The peak water levels near the time
of morning high tides for today through Thanksgiving are expected
to be near, or slightly exceed the October record.

By the end of this week, it is likely that the days with the four
highest water levels for San Diego will all be since July of this
year, along with 7 of the 10 highest. 


For La Jolla, the highest water level of 7.73 feet on Monday was
the third highest on record. It was also the second highest for 
November, exceeded by the 7.83 feet on November 25th, 2015. The 
peak water levels near the time of morning high tides for today 
through Thanksgiving are all expected to exceed the highest ever
recorded of 7.98 feet in late October of this year.

By the end of this week, it is likely that the three days with the
highest water levels ever recorded at La Jolla will be for today 
through Thanksgiving of this week, along with 7 of the 10 highest 
having occurred since July of this year.

At Scripps Pier, the water temperature of 73.2 F on Monday 
exceeded the long-term average for the date by 11.6 F. Water 
temperatures every day since late October have been the warmest on
record for the date, often by around 5 degrees F.

&&

.SKYWARN... 
Skywarn activation is not requested. However weather spotters are
encouraged to report significant weather conditions.
